native_mirror_before.title: The Whittaker functor from the relevant parabolic category-O summand
native_mirror_before.statement: On genuine parabolic O the Whittaker functor V is D_row Wh D_row, using restricted duality for the row-sum torus and the reflected head/tail identification; equivalently it is the appropriate continuous χ-coinvariant functor. It is exact on these U(m)-finitely-generated objects and intertwines finite tensoring, Casimir and flips. It is distinct from the subsequent Hecke quotient Hom_g(T,−). For admissible c define O_c^d from column-strict labels with nonnegative integral differences from each column's ground entries, P_c the ground simple projective-injective and T=P_c tensor V^tensor d. Then V(P_c)=C_c, V(T)=V_c^tensor d, and V(K(A)) is the simple W-module L(A) for Std labels and zero offStd. Nonintegral cosets have an explicit typed equivalence to products of the integral models; no arbitrary complex c is called an integral block of page16. The tensor compatibility is coherent and preserves x,s. After fixing the ground identification i_0:V(P_c)→C_c, the resulting compatible functor and j_d are unique up to the normalized unique natural isomorphism. Without this normalization scalar automorphisms prevent literal uniqueness.
native_mirror_before.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Use lower-central weights on U(m) to make its augmentation Rees algebra an image of the enveloping algebra of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra generated by y_i t^r, 0≤r≤w_i. PBW/Hilbert gives noetherianity; Rees submodule finiteness gives Artin–Rees for left ideals. Baer's criterion then proves the continuous dual union(U/I^k)* injective. Evaluation at1 identifies Hom_m(M,Eχ) with χ-finite functionals; the right action is λu(v)=λ(uv), so its E-valued expression is λ(u r v). The row-sum torus has χ weight0; finite U(m) generation makes these Hom spaces finite, giving exactness after restricted duality. Skryabin supplies the reflected head/tail W action. For nonintegral origins use the actual all-weight page13 adjoint-finite Verma theorem: tensor-projective Hom matrices identify the fixed-character Harish–Chandra category with the ordinary O linkage block. Ore twists across adjacent different integer cosets are exact by injective lowering and flat localization; their Verma highest vector F^−1v has s-dot weight, and the finite nilpotent tensor expansion identifies their invariant Hom matrices. Stable coset sorting preserves final Levi simple roots, hence the parabolic Serre subcategories and their largest generalized-Verma quotients. Shift a in a coset to a−cκ+n−nκ; choose common lower alphabet large enough, giving page16 column heights exactly q_j. For standard characters the Levi Weyl numerator is det(z_r^a_s) times the common factor product z_r^(n−1); the offsets cancel exactly. Classical Cauchy from Schur–Weyl identifies these nested-row minors with the actual16 highest projection, so offStd simple characters vanish. Its kernel is stable under residue operators; irreducibility of the highest component and nonzero ground force every Std image nonzero. Apply the two filtered-centralizer lifting arguments locally, independent of the later collector. T has only Std socle, so V is faithful on End T; surjectivity of the raw Hecke image gives End_g(T)^op=B_d. Factor exact V through the corner quotient Hom_g(T,−); its factor M tensor_B− is exact and faithful, hence M_B is a progenerator by projective-cover Nakayama. W_d=End_B(M) gives Morita and proves the Std images simple. The ZA polynomial-induction construction gives two-term add(T) copresentations of every projective; normalized tensor compatibility determines the natural isomorphism on T, then on all projectives via these kernels, then on all objects via projective presentations. Determinant shifts embed each finite coset chunk in a polynomial chunk. The Whittaker, HC, coset-label, quotient and Specht-corner local notes expand every step; no BG, KSX or W-simple-classification black box is required.

native_mirror_after.strategy: Assume AC. Define the continuous dual E_chi=union_n(U(m)/I_chi^n)^*. Give a lower-central adapted PBW generator weight w_i; I^n is spanned by monomials of weight>=n. Its Rees algebra is generated by y_i t^r,0<=r<=w_i; their finite Lie span has noetherian enveloping algebra by PBW/Hilbert basis. The finite generated Rees ideal gives J intersect I^n subset I^k J. For phi:J→E_chi choose a common I^k killing its generator images; extend the scalar functional phi(j)(1) on J/(J intersect I^n) to U/I^n. The resulting vector extends phi, proving Baer injectivity. Evaluation identifies Hom_m(N,E_chi) with scalar functionals killing I^nN; the right g action is (lambda.u)(v)=lambda(uv), hence on E-valued maps (F.u)(v)(r)=lambda(urv), not F(uv)(r). Finite PBW ad-m spans prove continuity. Right Skryabin makes its invariants exact; their covariant finite dual is V. Row-sum torus weights, not full Cartan, make these Hom spaces finite on genuine U(m)-finitely-generated parabolic O. Reflected finite-W path transposition proves the head/tail right model before using it. Compute finite-Levi characters by Weyl determinants with the exact constant offset; the nonzero flag-minor map onto the multiplicity-one highest constituent has the actual Fock projection kernel. Source simple classes L_O(A), not standards N(A), have zero character/image off Std; positivity and the nonzero ground class show no further kernel. Universal Casimir acts cyclotomically already on T; its image maps injectively to End_W(VT) because T has Std socle, giving End_g(T)^op=B. In a full generator algebra A with corner e cutting T, the Wh functor factors through e(-) as M tensor_B(-) by finite free presentations and the counit torsion kernel/cokernel. This factor is exact and faithful; projective-cover/Nakayama proves M_B projective, and faithfulness makes it a progenerator. Vust gives End_B(M)=Wd; hence Morita proves V(L_O(A)) simple precisely for Std. The ground normalization and balanced tensor compatibility determine the normalized comparison on the quotient presentations. All these arguments are written locally, not imported by citation.
